use: Style evidence only; never copy phrases, facts, numbers or identity.
method: Roster weights normalized over available eligible donors; equal mass per donor post; sentence mass equal within post. UTC cadence over observed scrape interval. Signature lift is weighted cluster document frequency divided by unweighted eligible all-donor document frequency (3-word EN / 4-character ZH n-grams, present in at least 2 cluster posts).

qualitative.cadence_notes: Deterministic stats show a median of about one post per day per donor. Activity concentrates in 13–17 UTC (US morning to midday) and stays meaningful into the US afternoon. It is lightest around 05–08 UTC. Roughly a quarter of posts are part of threads and nearly half carry media (charts/screenshots). Emoji appear in about one in nine posts, concentrated in a few donors. Sentences are short to medium (median ~11 words, interquartile ~5–21), and a mix of one-liners and multi-paragraph posts.

qualitative.variation_notes: Length ranges widely within the cluster. Some posts are bare one-liners pointing to a chart or link, and others are five- to six-paragraph mechanism explainers. Register shifts by donor. Some read like neutral reporting or wire relays, others like measured economist commentary, and others like loud alert-style or conviction-heavy trading takes with emoji and capitals. Most hooks are plain claims. Contrast turns, alert-flag headlines, questions, quotes and number-led openers each appear only in a minority of posts. The post-type mix leans toward data takes and view relays, with hot takes and mechanism explainers also common.
qualitative.judgment_style: Mostly assertive, with views stated as conclusions rather than questions. Several donors deliberately hedge, saying evidence is inconclusive in both directions, using conditional thresholds, or presenting a scenario as 'unlikely, but'. Data usually serves as support for a stated view rather than standing alone, though a notable share of posts relay a datum or another analyst's call with little added opinion. Conditional and causal phrasing is common in policy and rates posts. The more emphatic donors pair a single indicator with a strong directional call.
